title: My first shipped digital game - Veridian Contraption (A world simulator of Dubious Intent)
author: lerugray
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/6i2lgqi5c61h1.png?width=2400&format=png&auto=webp&s=dbbe0a6fd753aa0a5217d702b1242fdb40d81f03

Greetings all - 

Today I finished and shipped my first digital game (published about 30+ board wargames but have been working with AI to finally do video games, my first love) - while I designed the GDD and the scope of the game - claude was the engineer for the whole thing. Heavily inspired by the classic dwarf fortress, the illuminatius trilogy and kafka - Veridian Contraption is a very dense idle-first world simulation with a focus on prose generation and world-building - there is some limited, not required, player interaction where they can interact with the world, start guilds, levy quests, start a world changing event etc. The docs are very dense and a full manual is included, the soundtrack was written recorded and performed by me years ago back when I was a musician and the soundtrack ranges from baroque pop, chiptune and shoegaze. 

Feel free to ask me any questions about the development - selling it for 9.99 but if that is too expensive for you but this idea sounds really cool to you, shoot me a note and ill be happy to gift you a download code if you promise to actually play it and let me know how it goes. Took me about several months but I got distracted with other projects in between. Everything runs in a terminal via rust and ascii graphics, windows and mac versions shipped.

Link here: [https://conflict-simulations-llc.itch.io/veridian-contraption](https://conflict-simulations-llc.itch.io/veridian-contraption)

comments.author: mo_ngeri
comments.body:
This sounds genuinely ambitious for a first shipped digital game. The terminal/ascii direction is a nice choice too, since it puts the focus on simulation depth and writing instead of chasing visuals.
For future projects, I could even see something like hitem3d being useful if you ever want to turn parts of the world, factions, or creatures into lightweight visual assets without losing the weird procedural feel.

replies.author: lerugray
replies.body:
Thank you! I'm unfamiliar with hitem3d but I will take a look at it later. 


The UI/UX choice to limit things to rust I think was one of the better scoping choices I made, I did experiment with a tileset mode like DF and considered paying for art assets but frankly I couldn't afford any of the estimates (all reasonable for how much the game requires) - but like you mentioned it allowed me to really focus in and develop the systems design, being already versed in board wargames (sort of like analog programming for humans with lots of logic, edge cases detection and harmony between multiple systems) helped in terms of setting clear limits with claude as to what features I wanted. 


I dogfed a bunch of homespun tools I made in the creation of this, one of them being an mcp that downloads and summarizes research material and books from Anna's Archive and that helped a ton with the systemic depth being grounded in real research - I would encourage other game designers experimenting with AI to consider approaches that utilize AI to do the boring/tedious work of the design process and consider using UIs like the terminal, AIs natural training leads toward generic SaaS so creative work is best left done for humans. Sorry went off on a bit of a tangent there, too much coffee on my way to work.
